prompt:
CONCEPT: a citizen of the Oxygen Nation, of the Blood House. A female personification character with a red blood cell — a soft biconcave scarlet disc, drifting in a stream of many as her motif — the object reimagined as a woman in cloth and ornament that carry its materials, colors, shape and motifs. She does NOT hold, carry or wield the object; it is not a separate object. Both hands are ordinary human hands and hold nothing.
ELEMENT TRAITS of Oxygen (O) to carry in her design and the scene: breath and fire and rust in one: cool clear air as translucent cloth, bright combustion orange as accents, the quiet power to corrode, the deep blue of oceans and the green of forests; it is the element of life and burning. Palette: sea blue, forest green, clear white, combustion orange.
HOUSE TRAITS of Blood: blood as a living current carrying breath: bright arterial scarlet, branching vessel patterns like river deltas, a steady pulse, warm flushed pinks against deep venous blue; the circulating, life-carrying side of oxygen. Palette: arterial scarlet, venous blue, pulse pink, pale bone.
AGE: about twenty — a fresh young-adult face; no facial lines.
SILHOUETTE: petite, small-framed build; a bob with blunt straight bangs; bright red hair.
FACE — she must read as her own person at a glance, NOT the style's default pretty face and not a sister of the other characters: first impression — a cute, bright-eyed sweetness; warm beige skin; round face; large eyes — large round eyes, outer eye corners drooping downward; soft rounded brows; small button nose; small bow lips; azure-blue eyes; rosy flushed cheeks.
WORLD — STEAMPUNK: around 1800, a gas laboratory and a diving-bell harbour: glass bell jars, brass valves, an oxy-hydrogen limelight lamp, copper diving helmets, a lighthouse. Seen as if under a brass Victorian microscope: lens rings, slide glass and specimen labels as costume motifs. COSTUME (citizen, steampunk): her object leads — its silhouette, parts and materials must read at first glance in her outfit and headpiece, the object reimagined as cloth, leather and brass fittings; the steampunk era only sets the late-Victorian cut and the brass-and-leather finish. Steam, pipes and gauges in the scene; no modern plastic, no sci-fi. LIGHT: hazy gaslight and a smoky overcast sky, unless TIME & WEATHER says otherwise. HAIR: her hair is worn exactly as SILHOUETTE says — loose, long or cut as named; do not pin it up into a bun or tuck it under goggles or a hat unless SILHOUETTE says an updo.
STYLE: Polished 2.5D game key art with clean linework, anime facial design that keeps each character's own facial structure, eye proportions and skin tone instead of one house face, layered cel-to-soft shading and crisp costume and prop detail. Use a vivid, readable silhouette and campaign-quality lighting.
EXPOSURE (bold): her outfit opens to show skin — a deep open neckline with natural cleavage, bare shoulders or arms, a high slit or a short hem where the outfit allows; pieces stay symmetrical. Nothing slipped off. Chest and pelvis covered; no corset; keep the object's shape, material and palette.
OUTPUT: one character image that works as card art. Vertical 2:3 frame, full body with head and feet inside the frame with clear margins, face turned toward the camera (front or three-quarter). Standing, card-ready pose; the environment may be rich while her design stays fully readable.
EXPRESSION: one brow raised higher, head tilted, eyes wide and attentive, lips slightly parted.
BODY: a normal human body — one head, two arms and two legs, each joined at its natural joint. Hands and feet may be partly hidden by the pose or the frame.
ONE FIGURE ONLY. No second character, no living creature, no logo, no watermark, no speech bubble, no frame border. No text or numbers except her element's own chemical symbol (O) and atomic number (8) — those two may appear readably (engraved, stamped, glowing or on a sign or label); nothing else is written.
ANATOMY: natural adult proportions, both hands drawn correctly as hands. No extra limbs.
